name: Domain of Matthew III Csák
alt: Lord of the Váh and the Tatras

predecessors.name: Kingdom of Hungary
predecessors.text: '14 counties of the kingdom, and about 50 castles' around 1311; the lands now forming Slovakia

successors.name: Kingdom of Hungary
successors.text: '14 counties of the kingdom, and about 50 castles' around 1311; the lands now forming Slovakia

ledger.x: 1301: the Árpád line ends (Andrew III died on 14 January 1301) and Matthew III Csák, who inherited Komárno and Senica c.

c. 1311: his peak. 'By that time, 14 counties of the kingdom, and about 50 castles were under his and his followers' rule.' The page dates the extent only 'before Rozgony'; the region (Slovakia) is the Kingdom of Hungary dossier's reading.
25 June 1311: Matthew raids toward Buda (the cardinal excommunicated him on 6 July); royal forces liberate Sáros in 1311.
1315: Visegrád is 'occupied by Charles's forces'; John of Bohemia invaded his lands in May 1315 and defeated his troops at Holics.
1321: 'Matthew Csák's former domain was overtaken by the king's armies in a few months' time' after his death on 18 March 1321; his cousin Stephen Sternberg took over briefly.
1321: the domain falls to the royal armies within months of Matthew's death.
18 March 1321: Matthew III Csák dies; his domain does not outlive him.

wars.name: War of Charles I of Hungary against Matthew III Csák
wars.outcome: Charles I's army defeated Matthew and his allies at Rozgony on 15 June 1312, invaded his lands in 1314-1315 (John of Bohemia at Holics in May 1315, Visegrád) and overtook the domain in a few months after Matthew's death on 18 March 1321.

certainty.note: The page counts '14 counties' and 'about 50 castles', not a boundary; the lands were a patchwork of castles and followers.
